checked_claims.note: For a separating one-edge graph with six labelled legs, Aut(Gamma) is trivial, so the determinant-edge twist is vacuous. With rational coefficients, Cartan-Leray identifies degree-16 cohomology of the quotient stack with that of the ordered product atlas.
The relations g1+g2=6, n1+n2=8, and m1+m2=20, together with stability m_j>=3, give g_i<=6, 1<=n_i<=7, and m_i<=17. The stated bounds are attained.
Genus and 2g+n are non-increasing on vertices under stable-graph degeneration. A separating edge lowers 2g+n by at least one; a non-separating edge preserves 2g+n while lowering dimension by one.
For g<=6 and 2g+n<=17, the claimed bounds n<=c(g) follow for g in {0,3,4,5,6}. Genus 1 and genus 2 are correctly handled separately rather than being passed through the CKgP bounds.

In total Kunneth degree 16, odd bidegrees vanish because their smaller degree lies in {1,3,5,7}; mixed positive even degrees lie between 2 and 14 and are covered by THM-0002; the endpoint bidegrees use connectedness and the degree-16 hypothesis. No Gysin shift occurs.

Lemma A correctly combines the boundary-to-compact-to-open Borel-Moore sequence at degree 16, induction on the closed range g<=6 and 2g+n<=17, the genus-1 and genus-2 base results, CKgP in the remaining genera, the current dimension's Poincare twist, and semisimplicity of polarizable pure rational Hodge structures.
Every pair listed in RED-0001 has either g>=7 or 2g+n=18, whereas the entire induction remains in g<=6 and 2g+n<=17. Only the recorded seven-pair enumeration is used.

The claimed separating-edge conclusion follows: all invariant determinant-edge Kunneth summands in degree 16 are finite sums of Q(-8), degree-16 factors have n<=7 and avoid RED-0001, and mixed even factors lie in the published range. The non-separating component and global boundary-image theorem are expressly outside this theorem.

The proof uses the right-exact sequence H_16(hat-partial) -> H_16(Mbar) -> W_-16 H_16^BM(M) -> 0 and requires only that the boundary image is a quotient, not that the first arrow is injective.
The tabulated CKgP bounds c(0)=infinity, c(3)=c(4)=11, c(5)=7, and c(6)=5 are used only in the genera for which the induction's numerical range implies them.
For genus 1, all even compact cohomology is spanned by tautological algebraic classes. In degree 16, purity therefore gives an actual rational Hodge-structure decomposition into copies of Q(-8).
For genus 2, H^{2k}=RH^{2k} for k<=10 and all n; taking k=8 supplies the required degree-16 base case.

The cited results support the low even-degree Tate range, CKgP bounds, open-weight calculation, exact Borel-Moore sequence, and genus-1 input used in the proof.
Its odd-cohomology vanishing is used only in degrees 1, 3, 5, and 7, within the stated source range.

The proof applies W_-16 H_16^BM(M_{g,n}) = W_{2d-16} H^{2d-16}(M_{g,n})(d) using each current pair's dimension d. A codimension-(d-8) class has type Q(-(d-8)), and twisting by d gives Q(8), of weight -16.

The actual invoked result is semisimplicity of polarizable pure rational Hodge structures of fixed weight. It splits the weight-minus-16 extension as an honest Hodge-structure isomorphism, not merely after semisimplification.

proof_dependency_checks.note: The declared dependency supplies the verified geometric identification of one-edge components; the parser recovery from the subproblem identifier to ATT-0140 is consistent with the consumed artifact.
The normalized boundary is the distinguished-node stack. Lemma A repeats the same etale normal-crossings argument uniformly for the stable pairs in its induction.
The separating one-edge component is the quotient [Mbar_Gamma/Aut(Gamma)] with the stated vertex data, as required by the outer theorem and the generalized clutching step.

The cohomological contribution is the Aut(Gamma)-invariant determinant-edge summand. Over Q, quotient-stack homology is obtained through finite-group coinvariants, canonically equivalent to invariants; either is a Tate subquotient of the atlas homology.

strongest_attack: The strongest attack is that Lemma A requires H_16 of general quotient stacks [Mbar_Gamma/Aut(Gamma)], while ATT-0140 identifies the distinguished boundary specifically for (6,6) and expresses its contribution cohomologically using invariants and the determinant-edge character. After dualizing, invariants become coinvariants, and Aut(Gamma)=1 is false for non-separating one-edge graphs appearing in the induction. The attack does not succeed: Lemma A reruns the clutching and Cartan-Leray argument uniformly rather than extrapolating trivial automorphisms from (6,6). Over Q, finite-group invariants and coinvariants are canonically isomorphic through averaging and are Tate subquotients of the atlas group. The determinant character is a one-dimensional Hodge-trivial representation, so it cannot change Tate type. Thus the stack/coarse, invariants/coinvariants, and twist bookkeeping remains valid.
theorem_statement: Using a verified C66BAR-GRAPH identification of the one-edge separating components [Mbar_Gamma/Aut(Gamma)], prove that every Aut(Gamma)-invariant determinant-edge Kunneth summand in degree 16 is a finite direct sum of Q(-8). On the ordered product atlases, the only degree-16 factors that arise have n<=7 and lie outside RED-0001; even degrees <=14 are in the published tautological range. This theorem does not treat the non-separating component [Mbar_{5,8}/S_2] and does not conclude the campaign boundary-image theorem.
